question: What is the difference between `++i` and `i++`?

scenes.sub: Both add one. They differ in what they give back.
scenes.say: Plus plus i, versus i plus plus. Both add one to i. The difference is what the expression gives back.

scenes.head: Watch the values
scenes.say: Pre-increment, plus plus i, increments first, then returns the new value. So a and i are both six. Post-increment, j plus plus, saves a copy of the old value, increments j, and returns the copy. So b gets five, while j becomes six.

scenes.head: How a class implements them
scenes.say: You can see why in how a class implements them. Prefix increments and returns a reference to itself. No copy. Postfix must make a copy of the old object, increment, and return that copy. The extra int parameter is just a marker that means postfix.

scenes.head: Does it matter in loops?
scenes.say: For a plain int in a loop, the compiler makes both versions identical. For iterators or other objects, post-increment may create a copy you never use. So the habit is simple: write plus plus i, unless you actually need the old value.

lines: ++i: increment, then return the new value (by reference).
i++: copy the old value, increment, return the copy.
Default to ++i. Use i++ only when you need the old value.
scenes.say: Pre-increment: increment, then return the new value. Post-increment: copy the old value, increment, and return the copy. Default to plus plus i, and use i plus plus only when you need the old value.
